fields.title: 是 (shì)
fields.explanation: To be; used for identification or equivalence.
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘是 (shì)’ is the basic verb for ‘to be’ in Chinese. It links a subject with a noun or pronoun, indicating identity or equivalence. Unlike English, ‘是’ is not used to link a subject with an adjective (e.g., ‘I am happy’ is ‘我很高兴’, not ‘我是高兴’).
Structure: Subject + 是 + Noun/Pronoun
Examples: 我是学生。Wǒ shì xuéshēng. (I am a student.) 他是老师。Tā shì lǎoshī. (He is a teacher.)
Notes: ‘是’ is often omitted in sentences with adjectives. In negative sentences, use ‘不是 (bú shì)’.

fields.title: 有 (yǒu)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘有 (yǒu)’ means ‘to have’ or ‘there is/are’. It is used to indicate possession or existence.
Structure: Subject + 有 + Object
Examples: 我有一本书。Wǒ yǒu yī běn shū. (I have a book.)
Negative: Use ‘没有 (méiyǒu)’ for negation, not ‘不有’.
Example: 我没有钱。Wǒ méiyǒu qián. (I don’t have money.)

fields.title: 也 (yě)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘也 (yě)’ means ‘also’ or ‘too’. It is placed before the verb to indicate that the subject shares the same action or state as someone else.
Structure: Subject + 也 + Verb/Adjective
Example: 我也是老师。Wǒ yě shì lǎoshī. (I am also a teacher.)
Note: ‘也’ comes before the main verb, not at the end of the sentence.

fields.title: 不 (bù)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘不 (bù)’ is the standard negation word for verbs and adjectives in Chinese, except for ‘有 (yǒu)’.
Structure: Subject + 不 + Verb/Adjective
Example: 我不喜欢咖啡。Wǒ bù xǐhuān kāfēi. (I don’t like coffee.)
Note: For ‘have’, use ‘没有 (méiyǒu)’ instead of ‘不有’.
Negative with ‘是’: 我不是老师。Wǒ bú shì lǎoshī. (I am not a teacher.)

fields.title: 吗 (ma)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘吗 (ma)’ is a question particle placed at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question.
Structure: Statement + 吗？
Example: 你好吗？Nǐ hǎo ma? (Are you well?)
Note: The answer is usually ‘是’ (yes) or ‘不是’ (no), or a full sentence.

fields.title: 呢 (ne)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘呢 (ne)’ is a particle used at the end of a sentence to return a question or ask ‘how about…?’
Structure: Noun/Pronoun + 呢？
Example: 你呢？Nǐ ne? (And you?)
Note: Often used after answering a question to ask the same of the other person.

fields.title: 的 (de)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘的 (de)’ is a possessive particle used to indicate ownership or association.
Structure: Noun/Pronoun + 的 + Noun
Example: 这是我的书。Zhè shì wǒ de shū. (This is my book.)
Note: ‘的’ can sometimes be omitted in close relationships (e.g., 我妈妈 for ‘my mom’).

fields.title: 在 (zài)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘在 (zài)’ is used to indicate location or ongoing action.
Structure: Subject + 在 + Place
Example: 我在学校。Wǒ zài xuéxiào. (I am at school.)
Note: For ongoing actions, use ‘在’ before the verb: 我在吃饭。Wǒ zài chīfàn. (I am eating.)

fields.title: 会 (huì)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘会 (huì)’ means ‘can’ or ‘to know how to’. It is used for learned skills or abilities.
Structure: Subject + 会 + Verb
Example: 我会说汉语。Wǒ huì shuō Hànyǔ. (I can speak Chinese.)
Note: For physical ability, use ‘能 (néng)’. For permission, use ‘可以 (kěyǐ)’.

fields.title: 了 (le)
fields.explanation: Particle indicating completed action or change of state.
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘了 (le)’ is a particle used after a verb to indicate a completed action or a change of state.
Structure: Subject + Verb + 了
Example: 我吃了饭。Wǒ chī le fàn. (I have eaten.)
Note: ‘了’ can also be used at the end of a sentence to indicate a new situation or change.

fields.title: 正在 (zhèngzài)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘正在 (zhèngzài)’ is used before a verb to indicate an action is in progress, similar to the English ‘-ing’.
Structure: Subject + 正在 + Verb
Example: 我正在学习。Wǒ zhèngzài xuéxí. (I am studying.)
Note: ‘在’ alone can also indicate ongoing action.

fields.title: 要 (yào)
fields.explanation: To want; to be going to (future intention).
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘要 (yào)’ can mean ‘to want’ or ‘to be going to’ depending on context.
Structure: Subject + 要 + Verb/Object
Examples: 我要喝水。Wǒ yào hē shuǐ. (I want to drink water.) 我要去北京。Wǒ yào qù Běijīng. (I am going to Beijing.)
Note: For ‘want’, use ‘想 (xiǎng)’ for a softer tone.

fields.title: 可以 (kěyǐ)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘可以 (kěyǐ)’ is used to express permission or possibility.
Structure: Subject + 可以 + Verb
Example: 我可以进来吗？Wǒ kěyǐ jìnlái ma? (May I come in?)
Note: For ability, use ‘会 (huì)’ or ‘能 (néng)’.

fields.title: 因为…所以…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘因为…所以…’ is used to express cause and effect.
Structure: 因为 + Reason, 所以 + Result
Example: 因为下雨，所以我没去。Yīnwèi xiàyǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ méi qù. (Because it rained, I didn’t go.)
Note: Both parts are often used together, but ‘所以’ can be omitted in casual speech.
fields.example_pinyin: Yīnwèi xiàyǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ méi qù.
fields.example_en: Because it rained, I didn’t go.

fields.title: 比 (bǐ)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘比 (bǐ)’ is used to compare two things.
Structure: A + 比 + B + Adjective
Example: 他比我高。Tā bǐ wǒ gāo. (He is taller than me.)
Note: The adjective comes after the comparison.

fields.title: 得 (de)
fields.explanation: Used after a verb to indicate degree or result.
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘得 (de)’ is used after a verb to describe the manner or degree of the action.
Structure: Verb + 得 + Adjective/Complement
Example: 他说得很好。Tā shuō de hěn hǎo. (He speaks very well.)
Note: ‘得’ is different from ‘的 (de)’ and ‘地 (de)’.

fields.title: 就 (jiù)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘就 (jiù)’ is used to indicate quickness, earliness, or emphasis.
Structure: Subject + 一 + Verb + 就 + Result
Example: 我一到家就吃饭。Wǒ yī dào jiā jiù chīfàn. (I eat as soon as I get home.)
Note: ‘就’ can also mean ‘then’, ‘right away’, or ‘only’ depending on context.
fields.example_pinyin: Wǒ yī dào jiā jiù chīfàn.
fields.example_en: I eat as soon as I get home.

fields.title: 把 (bǎ)
fields.explanation: Used to emphasize the object of an action.
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘把 (bǎ)’ is used to bring the object of a verb before the verb, emphasizing what is affected by the action.
Structure: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + Other
Example: 请把门关上。Qǐng bǎ mén guān shàng. (Please close the door.)
Note: The object must be something known or specific. Often used with resultative or directional complements.

fields.title: 被 (bèi)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘被 (bèi)’ is used to form passive sentences, indicating the subject is affected by an action.
Structure: Subject + 被 + Doer + Verb + Other
Example: 他被老师批评了。Tā bèi lǎoshī pīpíng le. (He was criticized by the teacher.)
Note: The doer can be omitted if unknown or unimportant.
fields.example_en: He was criticized by the teacher.

fields.title: 越…越…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘越…越…’ expresses a progressive change or correlation.
Structure: Subject + 越 + Adj/Verb, 越 + Adj/Verb
Example: 天气越来越冷。Tiānqì yuè lái yuè lěng. (The weather is getting colder and colder.)
Note: Both parts use ‘越’ to show increasing degree.
fields.example_en: The weather is getting colder and colder.

fields.title: 虽然…但是…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘虽然…但是…’ is used to express contrast.
Structure: 虽然 + Clause 1, 但是 + Clause 2
Example: 虽然下雨，但是很热。Suīrán xiàyǔ, dànshì hěn rè. (Although it’s raining, it’s hot.)
Note: ‘但是’ can be replaced with ‘可是’ or ‘不过’.
Both clauses are usually present.

fields.title: 还是 (háishi)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘还是 (háishi)’ is used for ‘or’ in questions, offering a choice.
Structure: Option 1 + 还是 + Option 2
Example: 你喝茶还是咖啡？Nǐ hē chá háishi kāfēi? (Do you drink tea or coffee?)
Note: For statements, use ‘或者 (huòzhě)’.
‘还是’ can also mean ‘still’ in some contexts.
fields.example_en: Do you drink tea or coffee?

fields.title: 先…然后…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘先…然后…’ is used to describe sequential actions.
Structure: Subject + 先 + Action 1, 然后 + Action 2
Example: 我先吃饭，然后学习。Wǒ xiān chīfàn, ránhòu xuéxí. (I eat first, then study.)
Note: ‘然后’ means ‘then’ or ‘after that’.
‘先’ and ‘然后’ can be used together or separately.

fields.title: 一边…一边…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘一边…一边…’ is used to indicate two actions happening at the same time.
Structure: Subject + 一边 + Verb 1, 一边 + Verb 2
Example: 他一边唱歌一边跳舞。Tā yībiān chànggē yībiān tiàowǔ. (He sings while dancing.)
Note: Both actions are performed by the same subject.

fields.title: 过 (guò)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘过 (guò)’ is used after a verb to indicate past experience.
Structure: Subject + Verb + 过 + Object
Example: 我去过中国。Wǒ qù guò Zhōngguó. (I have been to China.)
Note: ‘过’ emphasizes the experience, not the time.

fields.title: 即使…也…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘即使…也…’ is used to express that something will happen or is true even under a certain condition.
Structure: 即使 + Condition, Subject + 也 + Result
Example: 即使下雨，我也去。Jíshǐ xiàyǔ, wǒ yě qù. (Even if it rains, I’ll go.)
Note: ‘即使’ introduces the hypothetical condition, ‘也’ introduces the result.
fields.example_en: Even if it rains, I’ll go.

fields.title: 不但…而且…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘不但…而且…’ is used to connect two related facts, emphasizing that not only the first is true, but also the second.
Structure: 不但 + Clause 1, 而且 + Clause 2
Example: 他不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞。Tā bùdàn huì chànggē, érqiě huì tiàowǔ. (He can not only sing, but also dance.)
Note: ‘而且’ can be replaced with ‘并且’ or ‘还’ in some contexts.
fields.example_cn: 他不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞。
fields.example_pinyin: Tā bùdàn huì chànggē, érqiě huì tiàowǔ.
fields.example_en: He can not only sing, but also dance.

fields.title: 由于…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘由于 (yóuyú)’ is used to introduce a reason or cause, often in formal contexts.
Structure: 由于 + Reason, Result
Example: 由于天气不好，比赛取消了。Yóuyú tiānqì bù hǎo, bǐsài qǔxiāo le. (Due to bad weather, the match was canceled.)
Note: Similar to ‘因为…所以…’, but more formal.
fields.example_cn: 由于天气不好，比赛取消了。
fields.example_pinyin: Yóuyú tiānqì bù hǎo, bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
fields.example_en: Due to bad weather, the match was canceled.

fields.title: 无论…都…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘无论…都…’ is used to express that the result will not change regardless of the condition.
Structure: 无论 + Condition, Subject + 都 + Result
Example: 无论你去哪里，我都跟你。Wúlùn nǐ qù nǎlǐ, wǒ dōu gēn nǐ. (No matter where you go, I’ll follow you.)
Note: ‘无论’ introduces the condition, ‘都’ introduces the result.
fields.example_cn: 无论你去哪里，我都跟你。
fields.example_pinyin: Wúlùn nǐ qù nǎlǐ, wǒ dōu gēn nǐ.
fields.example_en: No matter where you go, I’ll follow you.

fields.title: 既然…就…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘既然…就…’ is used to indicate that since a certain condition is true, then a certain result should follow.
Structure: 既然 + Known Situation, 就 + Result
Example: 既然你来了，就一起吃饭吧。Jìrán nǐ lái le, jiù yīqǐ chīfàn ba. (Since you’re here, let’s eat together.)
Note: ‘既然’ introduces the reason, ‘就’ introduces the result.
fields.example_cn: 既然你来了，就一起吃饭吧。
fields.example_pinyin: Jìrán nǐ lái le, jiù yīqǐ chīfàn ba.
fields.example_en: Since you’re here, let’s eat together.

fields.title: 只要…就…
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘只要…就…’ is used to express a sufficient condition.
Structure: 只要 + Condition, 就 + Result
Example: 只要努力，就会成功。Zhǐyào nǔlì, jiù huì chénggōng. (As long as you work hard, you’ll succeed.)
Note: ‘只要’ introduces the condition, ‘就’ introduces the result.
fields.example_en: As long as you work hard, you’ll succeed.

fields.title: 甚至 (shènzhì)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘甚至 (shènzhì)’ is used to emphasize something unexpected or extreme.
Structure: …，甚至 + Extreme Case
Example: 他很喜欢足球，甚至晚上做梦都在踢球。Tā hěn xǐhuān zúqiú, shènzhì wǎnshàng zuòmèng dōu zài tī qiú. (He likes football so much that he even dreams of playing it at night.)
Note: ‘甚至’ can be used before verbs, nouns, or clauses.
fields.example_cn: 他很喜欢足球，甚至晚上做梦都在踢球。
fields.example_pinyin: Tā hěn xǐhuān zúqiú, shènzhì wǎnshàng zuòmèng dōu zài tī qiú.
fields.example_en: He likes football so much that he even dreams of playing it at night.

fields.title: 并且 (bìngqiě)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘并且 (bìngqiě)’ is used to connect two verbs, adjectives, or clauses, meaning ‘and’ or ‘moreover’.
Structure: Clause 1, 并且 + Clause 2
Example: 他认真学习，并且帮助别人。Tā rènzhēn xuéxí, bìngqiě bāngzhù biérén. (He studies hard and also helps others.)
Note: ‘并且’ is more formal than ‘而且’ or ‘和’.
It can also mean ‘furthermore’ or ‘in addition’.
fields.example_cn: 他认真学习，并且帮助别人。
fields.example_pinyin: Tā rènzhēn xuéxí, bìngqiě bāngzhù biérén.
fields.example_en: He studies hard and also helps others.

fields.title: 怎么 (zěnme)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘怎么 (zěnme)’ is used to ask about the manner or method.
Structure: 怎么 + Verb
Example: 怎么说？Zěnme shuō? (How do you say?)
Note: The answer is usually a full sentence.

fields.title: 哪里 (nǎlǐ)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘哪里 (nǎlǐ)’ is used to ask about location.
Structure: 哪里 + Noun
Example: 哪里？Nǎlǐ? (Where?)
Note: The answer is usually a place.

fields.title: 什么 (shénme)
fields.detailed_explanation:
‘什么 (shénme)’ is used to ask about the identity or nature.
Structure: 什么 + Noun
Example: 什么？Shénme? (What?)
Note: The answer is usually a noun.
